newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on growth prospects.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on growth prospects.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher amid short-covering Monday, spurred by more evidence of rising growth.
"Many people covered shorts this session," after the FRB broke through 85-1/4 said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.36 to 121.15, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 gained 3/4 to 85-6/8.
"The signs of an economic rebound are creating a favorable climate for investors in the medium-term, although high price levels mean spectacular gains are not expected," said another trader.
The Economy Ministry announced late Monday industrial production rose 12.5 percent in October from the same month a year earlier and advanced 4.1 percent from September.
Earlier, the FIEL private consultancy estimated an 11.3 percent increase in industrial production in October.

"Many banks are recommending Argentine bonds on the rebound in growth," commented the first trader. And the improving fundamentals are paying off, with Argentine Brady bonds outperforming most Latin American markets this session.
But the first trader said the FRB had difficulty breaking through the 86 level, a point it could struggle with in coming sessions.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.65 percent from 6.0 percent.
